title: Minimum Time to Build Blocks
summary: Given a list of blocks with specified build times, determine the minimum time required to build all blocks.
statement: Given a list of blocks with specified build times, determine the minimum time required to build all blocks. Initially, there is one worker, and the cost of splitting one worker into two is given as an integer. A worker can either split into two workers, increasing the total number of workers by one, or build a block and then go home. Both actions have associated costs.
constraints: 1 <= len(blocks) <= 1,000; build and split times are positive.
One worker may either build one block or spend split time becoming two workers; parallel actions finish when the slower branch finishes.
Return the least elapsed time to finish every block.
hints: A split creates the two branches of a parallel schedule.
Combine the two quickest remaining jobs because delaying either cannot improve the maximum finish time.
Min-heap jobs; remove the smallest, add split to the next smallest, and reinsert it.
This is the reverse construction of an optimal binary worker tree; the final heap value is its makespan.
editorial: This is the reverse construction of an optimal binary worker tree; the final heap value is its makespan.

tests.explanation: One worker builds the only block in one unit.
Splitting takes five units, then parallel builds take two more, totaling seven.
